title: Track and Drift Questions
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 3. Q1–12 are the book's worked examples turned into choices (answer = the book's working); Q13–16 key from the printed grid, PDF p. 249

13.q: Compass heading 270°, deviation 2° W, variation 30° E, relative bearing 316°. What is the QDR?

16.q: An aircraft at 9000 ft flying towards a station can receive VHF R/T from a ground station 1600 ft AMSL at a distance of about:

1.q: An aircraft is homing to a station on 090° (M) with 10° starboard drift. What does the RBI show?

2.q: An aircraft is homing to a station on 360° (M) with 15° port drift. What does the RBI show?

3.q: An aircraft is flying away from a station on 270° (M) with 15° port drift. What does the ADF read?

4.q: An aircraft is flying away from a station on a magnetic heading of 030°. The RBI shows 185°. Track and drift?

5.q: An aircraft is flying away from a station on a track of 200° (M) with 10° starboard drift. Heading and RBI?

6.q: An aircraft is flying away from a station on heading 270° (M), making good a track of 260°. RBI and drift?

7.q: After 2 h at 80 kt GS on heading 090°, the ADF shows 168°; 2 h remain to the station. Heading to steer for the station?

8.q: After 180 NM on heading 200°, the ADF shows 186°; 120 NM remain to the destination. New heading to the station?

9.q: Constant heading, 12° S drift, track made good 5 NM left of and parallel to the airway centreline. NDB on the centreline 30 NM ahead. RBI? (assume heading 090°)

10.q: Constant heading, 12° P drift, track made good 5 NM right of the centreline. NDB on the centreline 30 NM behind. ADF reading? (assume heading 090°)

11.q: Constant heading, 8° S drift, track made good 5 NM right of the airway centreline. NDB on the centreline 30 NM ahead. ADF reading? (assume heading 090°)

12.q: Constant heading, 5° S drift, track made good 5 NM left of the centreline. NDB on the centreline 30 NM ahead. ADF reading? (assume heading 090°)

ex.4: MBT = 185 + 030 = 215, so MBF (track) 035; track right of heading: 5° S.
ex.6: MBT 080; RB = 080 − 270 + 360 = 170; track left of heading: 10° P.
ex.7: MBT = 258 → track 078, drift 12° P. 160 NM flown: off-track 32 NM → TE 12°, closing angle 12°. Heading = 090 + 12 + 12 = 114.
ex.8: MBT 026 → track 206, drift 6° S. TE 6° → 18 NM off; closing angle 18/120 × 60 = 9°. Correction 15°: 200 − 15 = 185.
ex.9: Required track 102; 5 NM in 30 NM = 10°; NDB is right of the track: MBT 112; RB = 112 − 090 = 022.
ex.10: Track 078 + 10 = 088 from the NDB; MBT 268; RB = 268 − 090 = 178.
ex.11: Required track 098, the NDB is 10° left: MBT 088; RB = 088 − 090 = −2 → 358.
ex.14: 075 T + 10 W = 085 M track; drift 7° right means head 7° left: heading 078; RB = 085 − 078 = 007.
